gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-ugarit: Ornate and bookish, Almendra Display keeps its letters open and its lowercase tall. Noto Sans Ugaritic sits beneath it as a plain sans, its capitals barely taller than its lowercase, so the two read smoothly together.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-vai: Audiowide draws every stroke at a single thickness, its letters set apart like tiles with wide gaps between. And Noto Sans Vai gives its words a solid, blocky texture, so a larger heading over modest body text feels natural.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-meroitic: Spiky, dark and a bit menacing, Eater spaces its letters wide and keeps its ascenders stubby. But Noto Sans Meroitic is the one you can see through, its lowercase filling the line almost like capitals.
gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-vithku: Almendra Display brings an ornate, literary hand, with letters that never pinch shut and a lowercase that stands tall. Noto Sans Vithkuqi handles the plain work instead, keeping its throats open and its capitals only a small step above the lowercase.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Audiowide has a futuristic look, with strokes that never swell or thin and a lowercase that towers over its capitals. Noto Sans Wancho counters with chunky, pressed-hard lowercase.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-modi: Eater looks dark and aggressive, its thin strokes staying sturdy beside the stems and its letters spaced wide apart. But Noto Sans Modi does the quiet job, with daylight inside every curve and capitals close in height to the lowercase.
gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-warang: Literary and ornate, Almendra Display never pinches its letters shut. Noto Sans Warang Citi lays out words as solid blocks with wide channels into each counter, so shrinking the heading or enlarging this body would soften the difference.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-yi: Audiowide holds its stroke width constant, with tile-like letters spaced by wide gaps. Noto Sans Yi has a deep lowercase midsection and rounds left unsealed, which gives the pair a crisp, modern texture.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-mono: Dark, spiky and wide-spaced, Eater means business. Noto Sans Mono gives sturdy, tall lowercase and generous openings in every curve, so the page feels grounded after the menace of the heading.
gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-zanaba: Approachable and crisp, Noto Sans Zanabazar Square soars in its x-height. Over many lines its wide gaps keep words distinct, while Almendra Display adds an ornate, literary note above without crowding it.
